newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Superconductor holder seeks management change.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Superconductor holder seeks management change.

text.p: A major sharheolder of Illinois Semiconductor Corp, a wireless communications product developer, said Monday he was seeking to have the company name a new chief executive officer.

Sheldon Drobny, a private investor, said he has proposed that Illinois Suyperconductor Corp name Semar Sirazi as chief executive officer, president and chairman of the board, adding that Sirazi has purchased and currently holds more than 35,000 shares of the common stock of Illinois Superconductor.
Sirazi is vice president and general manager of the Cable Access Business Unit at 3Com Corp, having worked at U.S. Robotics Corp when it was acquired by 3COM, Drobny said.
Drobny beneficially held 8.3 percent of Illinois Semiconductor's stock as of its 1996 10-K annual report filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Drobny said in a news release he has no doubts about Illinois Superconductor's technology.

"Unfortunately, ISC has failed to communicate its success to the marketplace and the public," Drobny said. "For example, although ISC's sales continue to increase, it refuses to identify the purchasers, or the number of filters sold in each location. We believe that this is material information that the investing public has a right to know."
Drobny also said he believes directors of the company should be significant shareholders, and that he has amended his 13D filing with the SEC to reflect this belief and to propose management changes.
A spokesman for Illinois Superconductor was not immediately available.
Illinois Superconductor shares closed at 10-1/4 Friday.
